note: Work: the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) Act, No. 2 of 2021 (certified 18 January 2021) redefines a 'child' in section 34 of the principal Act (No. 47 of 1956) as a person under sixteen, raises the ages in section 9 from fifteen to sixteen and repeals section 10; the Shop and Office Employees (Amendment) Act, No. 1 of 2021, likewise moves fourteen to sixteen. The principal Act's bar on employing a child (section 13) wasn't read in its own text, so 16 as the general minimum is my reading of the amendment; the 1956 Act's exceptions (family agricultural work, and any for entertainment under the Children and Young Persons Ordinance) weren't read, and the form holds performers barred below 16 (my reading, to check). A 2026 amending bill (Bill 44 of 2026, found by search, not read) may change section 7. Read from LankaLAW's compilation of the 2021 Acts (documents.gov.lk, the Government Printer, returned 404 for the Act's URL). Majority: the Age of Majority Ordinance wasn't found; left null. Service: no conscription law was found; left null.

sources.said: “child” means a person who is under the age of sixteen years;” ... by the substitution for the words “fifteen years” of the words “sixteen years”
